text:
A: Here he is! The Arsenal man. Alright, mate?
B: Alright. Who told you that?
A: Gemma. Said you was gaming on your lunch at four o'clock.
B: Course she did. It was a late lunch.
A: I'm not judging, mate, I'd do the same. Darren, by the way.
B: Craig. You're the forklift one, yeah?
A: Was. Back's gone. Eighteen months signed off now. I'm on the Universal Credit, seeing a work coach, all that. Looking at van driving, security, caretaker, anything that doesn't mean twisting round on a counterbalance all day. Honestly, I'd sweep the car park if it paid the rent.
B: Right. Have you thought about the office side? Warehouse admin, inventory control. You know the floor, that's half of it. Most of the people doing that have never set foot on a shift.
A: Me, in an office? I'd lose the paperwork in a week, mate. I lost paperwork on the forklifts, and that was one sheet.
B: They're mostly screens now. Scan it, click it, done.
A: Yeah, well. I'm not great on computers.
B: Nobody is. That's why I've got a job.
A: Ha! Fair. What is it you do, then?
B: Write the software warehouses run on. The thing on the scanner that tells you where to go.
A: You're joking. So it's you, is it? The one that freezes on a Friday night with forty trailers waiting?
B: Probably not me. Usually somebody's put the server in a cupboard.
A: Mate, ours was in a cupboard. With the mop.
B: There you go.
A: Unbelievable. So who's your team, then, apart from Arsenal bottling it?
B: That's it. Just Arsenal. Mostly the highlights, if I'm honest.
A: Highlights! You're not a fan, you're a viewer. I'm Bristol City, loosely, but Bridgwater United properly. Stood in the rain for them since I was eight.
B: Sounds miserable.
A: It is. Best thing in the world. You play anything?
B: Five-a-side for a bit. The group chat got too organised, so I stopped going.
A: Too organised! I've never heard that one. I do darts now, pub team, Thursdays. Back permitting.
B: Any good?
A: Decent average on a good night. Thursday wasn't a good night. Lost by one leg, and the bloke's double sixteen bounced out and they gave it him anyway.
B: How does a bounce-out count?
A: It doesn't! That's what I've been saying since Thursday, mate. Nobody'll listen.
B: Yeah, that's daft. Get it on video next time.
A: See, you're alright, you. Said you looked a grumpy sod in your photo.
B: I get that a lot. It's just my face.
A: Join the club. What do you do when you're not fixing cupboards, then?
B: Gaming. Bit of home server stuff. Smart lights that never quite work.
A: Never quite work. I've had a moped in the back yard three years, "nearly finished." Kerry wants it gone.
B: Becky says the same about my bike. What's wrong with it?
A: Carburettor, I reckon. Or me. Probably me.
B: Probably the carb. Send us a picture and I'll—
